title: Frequently asked questions
content: **Q: Can I use LiveSync with multiple instances of CLO or Marvelous Designer, or multiple Unreal Engine instances?** A: Unfortunately LiveSync is designed to work with a single instance of CLO or Marvelous Designer along with one Unreal Editor. **Q: Can I use LiveSync and EveryWear together?** A: EveryWear and LiveSync are separate pipelines and cannot be used together. However, you can still bring garments exported with EveryWear into Unreal Engine by simply importing the FBX file. **Q: When I send garments to Unreal Engine, the looks are different. Is it possible to make them look same?** A: Due to inherent differences in rendering systems, 'similar' looks are achieved, but it is nearly impossible to achieve identical looks. If you use CLO's V-Ray renderer, you can use [UE5's Path Tracer](https://docs.unrealengine.com/5.3/en-US/path-tracer-in-unreal-engine/) as both utilize raytracing. **Q: Which texture maps are sent to Unreal Engine via LiveSync?** A: The following texture maps are gathered and sent to Unreal Engine: * Base color map * Normal map * Roughness map * Metallic map * Reflection map * Opacity map
content_description: This web page provides essential information about the functionality and limitations of LiveSync with CLO, Marvelous Designer, and Unreal Engine, including compatibility, rendering differences, and texture map transmission.

title: What is LiveSync?
content: **LiveSync** is a bridge which connects CLO and Unreal Editor (CLO LiveSync), or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Editor (MD LiveSync), and aims to shorten workflows requiring rendering in Unreal Engine. This is particularly useful if your workflow involves CLO or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine, however, it is worth noting that intermediate process of using other software products may be eventually eliminated as LiveSync continues to get updated. Traditional workflows involve repetitive yet tedious and destructive process of exporting garments as desired file formats and importing the results in Unreal Engine, since users need to manually manage properties expressing realistic garments in CLO or Marvelous Designer. This is caused by limitations of using specific file formats, and you can only imagine fatigue accumulated from doing file exports, imports, and potentially redoing everything if design for garments needs to be adjusted in CLO or Marvelous Designer. By establishing a direct bridge, CLO and Marvelous Designer can communicate with Unreal Editor, **eliminating needs for file exports and imports**. LiveSync features and workflows can be found in [Using LiveSync via CLO/MD LiveSync Editor](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304301544473) and [MetaHuman workflow with LiveSync](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304302752537). ### Tutorials & Walkthroughs For comprehensive guidance, refer to these two tutorial videos on CLO/MD LiveSync. The first is an excellent walkthrough by **Matt Workman** (Cinematography Database) using LiveSync 2.1.0, Unreal Engine 5.6, and MetaHuman. The second is our official tutorial demonstrating the workflow for earlier versions of CLO/MD LiveSync (pre-2.0.0) and Marvelous Designer 2024.0. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CoYfZP5GEJM YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hB9S-rYm98M
content_description: Discover how LiveSync revolutionizes garment design workflows by seamlessly connecting CLO and Marvelous Designer with Unreal Engine, eliminating tedious file exports and imports for a more efficient creative process.

content: **Objective ** Create Scene&Prop items by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **Required & Recommended **Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling a Prop. **[Required]** * "Prop" refers to any prop mesh that goes into the Scene/Stage. * The file should not include anything other than Prop meshes. (e.g. Select Prop Mesh only when exporting) * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * In the Description, the following information about the product must be provided. (1) UV MAP unwrapping status O or X **[Recommended]** * It is recommended to apply the same material to the part using the same material. * UVs should be unwrapped so that they do not overlap so that customers can use a variety of textures. * If mesh and the normal map have the same location and direction, it may cause overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Be careful not to overlap the mesh. * If the two vertices are overlapping, please weld them together. * For the complex graphic pattern, please use the Normal map. (e.g., logo and pattern) * It is recommended to use textures with a maximum size of 2048 pixels. * The scanned OBJ is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. * It is recommended to add a wire to express the sharp edge. **Details** **1\. title: Creating Motion (MTN) - Auto Conversion
content: **Objective** Create a Motion file (.mtn) using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. Converting and redistributing motions downloaded for free or purchased from other platforms is prohibited to protect the original creators' rights. **Please create and use a motion file (.mtn) for personal use only.** * Examples: Mixamo, DAZ 3D, Reallusion-Actorcore, Unreal Marketplace, Artstation Marketplace, Sketchfab, etc **1\. How to Create a motion file (.mtn) via auto-convert features** * Manual - Auto Convert to Avatar ([CLO](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055227373-Automatic-Rigging-Converter)/ [Marvelous Designer](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358210639897-Auto-Convert-to-Avatar-Ver-2024-0)) * Manual - Auto Convert to Motion ([CLO](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/13249323691929-Auto-Convert-to-Motion-ver-7-1)) * **※ Note: 'Auto Convert to Motion' is currently compatible with Mixamo only.** 1-1. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with the CLO avatar. 1-2. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with a custom avatar. **1-1. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with the CLO Avatar** When using the CLO avatar, you can skip the 'Auto Convert to Avatar' and move directly to 'Auto Convert to Motion.' 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. 2. From the main menu, click on **File > Open > Avatar**, or click on **Avatar in the Library.** 3. Load your desired CLO Avatar. 4. From the main menu, click on **Avatar >**[**Auto Convert to Motion**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/13249323691929-Auto-Convert-to-Motion-ver-7-1) 5. Select the gender and the motion file (.fbx) you have created or downloaded. Click **'Convert'** when ready.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775587110169) 6. Save the motion file (.mtn) by clicking **'Save'** when the auto-conversion is finished.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775618995097) **※ Note: If you changed the CLO avatar's body shape, please save the avatar size file (.avs) in advance so you can easily match the size of the dummy CLO avatar displayed during 'Auto Convert to Motion' to your avatar.** **![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775578625817)** **1-2. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with a Custom Avatar** When using a custom avatar, you must run the "Auto Convert to Avatar" before applying any motion files (.mtn). 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. 2. From the main menu, click on **Avatar > **[**Auto Convert to Avatar**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055227373-Automatic-Rigging-Converter)**![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775587633433)** 3. Set the options and adjust the dummy CLO avatar's body shape using Avatar Editor while the 'Auto Convert to Avatar' is on. (Click the [**LINK**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=ZgcPIf0LqoSbaDQN&t=1746) to check the tutorial.) 4. Select the gender and the motion file (.fbx) you have created or downloaded. Click 'Convert' when ready.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775587110169) 6. Save the motion file (.mtn) by clicking **'Save'** when the auto-conversion is finished.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775618995097) **※ Note: Please adjust the dummy CLO avatar displayed during 'Auto Convert to Motion' using the Avatar Editor to match your custom avatar's body shape.** **2\. Create a Thumbnail Image** You can upload a thumbnail for the motion file in an image or an animation. If you are creating the thumbnail as an animation, please use approximately **100 to 200 frames** from the entire motion sequence for the thumbnail. **※ Tip** : you can make the motion thumbnail longer as long as GIF/WebP animations don't exceed **50 megapixels** (the sum of sizes of all frames). * * IK Mapping feature is available starting from CLO 2025.0 and Marvelous Designer 2025.0. **Objective** With the IK Mapping feature, you can create motion (.mtn) and pose (.pos) files, as well as compatible avatars (.avt), that can be freely applied to various avatars. * **Notes** * There must be no duplicate joint names within the FBX file. If duplicate names are present, the IK Mapping feature may not function correctly. * For avatars that differ from the Humanoid structure, such as creatures or quadruped avatars, the IK Mapping results may not align with expectations. Therefore, it is recommended to use bipedal, Humanoid-based avatars. * The more similar the '**Target** ' Avatar's T-Pose is to the standard pose, the more consistent and higher the quality of results when applying Poses (.pos) and Motions (.mtn). * You can check the CLO Avatar's T-Pose in the library. **1\. How to use IK Mapping** To fully use the IK Mapping, both 'T-Pose' and 'IK Joint' settings are required. At least all joints marked as '**Required** ' must be mapped. * **1-1. IK Mapping Workflow** 1. Import the avatar FBX or animated avatar FBX file. 2. From the top Menu, Avatar > Avatar Editor > Select '**IK Mapping** ' Tab![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775595775897) 3. Adjust the Avatar's joints to set the T-Pose. 4. Click the ‘**Set T-Pose** ’ button.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775595955865) 5. Click the ‘**Auto Mapping** ’ button or manually connect each joint.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775643319833)
``` *** Auto Mapping-Supported Avatar Platforms Avatars from the following platforms can be automatically mapped using the 'Auto Mapping' button: ** **- DAZ** – Genesis 8, Genesis 9 **- Reallusion** **- Mixamo** **- Unreal Metahuman** **- Avatars with the same joint structure and names as CLO avatars.**
``` **1-2. Manual IK Mapping** When mapping joints manually, it’s essential to understand the name and function of each joint and connect them accurately to the corresponding body part. Please refer to the image below to verify the position and function of each joint and then connect them accordingly. Joints labeled in red in the image represent the required joints; be sure to map all of them. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775611740441) * * **Head** : Head Part * **Neck** : Neck Part * **Spine1, Spine2** : Upper Parts of the spine. * **Waist** : The first joint of the spine in the waist area. * **Hips** : The central joint that connects the avatar's spine and both legs or thighs (parent bone of the spine and leg structures) * **Left/Right Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist** : Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist * **Left/Right Hip, Knee, Ankle, Foot** : Left/Right Leg Connection (Hip), Knee, Ankle, Foot * Only one roll joint can be mapped for arms and legs, so if multiple roll joints are used, please select and map the roll joint with the most significant influence, considering the movement. **Neck and Spine** IK Mapping supports 10 neck joints and 9 spine joints. The neck and spine joints are numbered sequentially from bottom to top. The smaller the number, the closer it is to the hips; the larger the number, the closer it is to the head. Please refer to the image below to check the location and order of each joint and map them accurately in sequence. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775611903641) **Neck** * * The Neck is the first skeletal joint following the spine. * From the Neck to the Head, joints must be mapped in order as **Neck1** , **Neck2** , **Neck3** , without skipping any numbers. * Additional neck joints (Neck1~Neck9) are not required for IK Mapping. If your avatar contains additional neck joints, you can optionally choose to connect or map them. **Spine** * * The first spine joint must be mapped to the Waist. * From the Waist up to the position where the shoulder joints connect, map the joints in sequence as **Spine1** , **Spine2** , **Spine3** , without skipping any numbers. * Additional spine joints (Spine1~Spine9) are also not required by IK Mapping. If your avatar contains extra spine joints, you may optionally connect or map them. **Shoulder** IK Mapping supports both basic shoulder joints (Left/Right Collar) and extra shoulder joints (Left/Right Collar Extra). * Please refer to the image below to identify the position of each shoulder joint and connect them accurately to match your avatar. * ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775612142873) * The Left/Right Collar Extra joints are positioned between the essential Collar (Left/Right) and the Shoulder joints. * These extra shoulder joints are not required for IK Mapping and can be mapped optionally if your avatar has them. **Hands and Feet** IK Mapping supports a maximum of 6 fingers and toes per hand or foot (i.e., Thumb through Pinky, plus an extra finger or foot). Each finger and toe can have a maximum of 4 joints labeled **A** , **B** , **C** , and **D** , with D representing the tip joint. * Please refer to the image below to check the position and names of each joint in the hands and feet, then connect or map them accordingly to your avatar. * ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775661160985) ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775661366169) * Finger and toe joints must be mapped in the order **A** , **B** , **C** , and **D** without skipping any. * Hand and Foot nodes are not mandatory joints in IK Mapping, but you may connect/map them optionally if you want the fingers and toes to be retargeted. *** After manual mapping, please double-check that all joints have been correctly connected.** ### 2\. How to save Avatar (.avt) / Pose (.pos) / Motion (.mtn) After completing the IK Mapping setup, save the Avatar (.avt), Motion (.mtn), and Pose (.pos) files with IK Mapping data. * These saved files contain embedded IK Mapping data, allowing them to be compatible and utilized together without any additional settings. * * **2-1. In the 3D window, click on the avatar, then right-click > select '**Reset Joint**.' 2. Make sure the avatar has transitioned to the initial pose. 3. Saving Pose (.pos) / Motion (.mtn)** 1. From the top menu, click Animation > select '**Animation Editor**.' ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775654137113) 2. In Animation Editor, right-click and select '**Clamp Range to Active Frames** ' to automatically set the animation playback range from the start to the end frame. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775613284377) 3. From the top menu, go to File > Save As > select '**Joint Motion** ' or '**Pose** ' to save the motion (.mtn) or pose (.pos) file. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775645905049) **2-3. Extra Features for Pose (.pos) / Motion (.mtn) Editing** * After applying a pose (.pos) or motion (.mtn) following the IK Mapping setup, specific joint movements may appear unnatural. * In such cases, the '**Offset Joint'** and '**Move to Ground'** features can help adjust the animation more naturally. * These two features apply uniformly across all animation frames. Offset Joint values can be checked and edited in the '**Offset Joint'** window even after the avatar (.avt) file is saved. * * * **Offset Joint** The '**Offset Joint'** allows you to adjust offset values when specific joint angles appear unnatural after applying a motion, enabling you to create better joint angles. **How to Use** * 1. In Animation Editor, right-click on an animation frame and select '**Offset Joint**.' 2. Click the joint you want to adjust. 3. In the Offset Joint window, set the offset value to adjust to the joint angle. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775597936793) ### Move to Ground The '**Move to Ground** ' automatically adjusts the height when the Motion or Pose is applied after IK Mapping in cases where the avatar’s feet are floating above the ground (Grid). This allows the feet to touch the ground naturally. **How to Use** 1. 1. Check if the avatar is floating above the ground (Grid). 2. In Animation Editor, right-click on an animation frame and select '**Move to Ground**.' 3. Check if the avatar’s feet are touching the ground.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775662707737) ※ Note: The '**Move to Ground** ' determines the ground position based on the current frame when it is executed. Therefore, please use this feature on the frame where the avatar’s feet should be in contact with the ground. * ### **3\. Errors and Solutions** If a pop-up message labeled ‘**No Matching Avatar** ’ appears after applying the Motion or Pose file following the IK Mapping setup, please check the following items: * Please make sure the T-Pose is set in the IK Mapping tab. * In the IK Mapping tab, please make sure all joints are properly connected under the '**Required** ' section. ![image \(28\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775598261913) **4\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** When uploading the AVT, MTN, or POS file to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers. * If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775662981913) **1\. UPLOAD (Mandatory)** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE (Mandatory)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the **DEFAULT TITLE**. **3\. DESCRIPTION** Please provide customers with detailed file information. **For Avatar:** * AVATAR HEIGHT (Scale Unit) * BUST CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * HIP CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * Presence of the JOINTS * Compatibility with CLO's AVATAR SIZING EDITOR * Compatibility with CLO's default AVATAR ASSETS * Presence of the Fitting Suit * Presence of the IK Mapping (CLO/Marvelous Designer 2025) **For Pose / Motion:** * Presence of the IK Mapping (CLO/Marvelous Designer 2025) * For Avatar (.avt), Motion (.mtn), or Pose (.pos) files that do not contain IK Mapping data, please provide the file name or download link of the avatar compatible with those files. **4\. TAGS** '**TAGS** ' is a target keyword that helps customers search for and amplify the reach of your content. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **5\. ATTACHMENT** You can attach files related to the Avatar (.AVT), Pose (.POS), or Motion (.MTN). However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to '**ATTACHMENT** ' are being used. **6\. ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can also add images that highlight the characteristics of the AVT (.AVT), Pose (.POS), or Motion (.MTN). **7\. THUMBNAIL** Register an image that well showcases the characteristics of the Avatar (.AVT), Pose (.POS), or Motion (.MTN). title: What is EveryWear?
content: **EveryWear** is a feature package that optimizes garments made in CLO and Marvelous Designer for digital spaces like gaming, metaverse, and entertainment. Subscribers of CLO and Marvelous Designer can access these features for free during the beta phase. For additional information, please visit our [**website**](https://connect.clo-set.com/everywear). **EveryWear** will significantly reduce your time and costs by automating repetitive tasks. Here is a list of features that will streamline the process of converting your 3D garment to the digital space. **#1. Fitting** Auto Fitting automatically adjusts 2D patterns and 3D garment to fit the size/body of the avatar. It allows creators to easily modify clothing designed for different avatar sizes/body to fit the other avatars in different sizes. **#2. Rigging** Rigging involves attaching 3D garment to a character and defining how it moves and behaves in real-time application like video games. It allows creators to significantly reduce the time required for rigging. **#3. Texture Baking** Texture baking is to capture and transfer information from high-resolution 3D garment to 2D texture maps. It allows creators to improve the efficiency and and increase the realism of 3D garments. **#4. Level of Detail** Level of Detail (LoD) involves creating different versions of a 3D character and dynamically selecting which one to render based on the viewer's distance. Creators don't need to worry about LoD, as it automatically generates the other levels based on the creator's original design. **EveryWear Tutorial** ****

title: Creating Avatar
content:
**Objective ** Create an Avatar by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **1\. Creating AVATAR** Create an Avatar in other 3D software. Avatar files should be created in OBJ/FBX/GLB/GLTF formats, and avatars with joints are recommended to be in FBX formats. For avatars with textures applied, please make sure to check 'Embed Media' in the Export Option. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775561103897) **※ Note:** The following Skinning Methods are not compatible with CLO and Marvelous Designer: **Dual Quaternion and Weight Blend.** **Required & Recommended** ※ Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling Avatar. ** ****[Required]** * All mesh must be created in Y-axis(up) environment. * You can import the following formats into Avatar Type: OBJ, FBX, GLB, and GLTF. * All mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. **[Recommended]** * For the best outfit-fitting performance, it is strongly recommended to create an avatar in either an A-pose or a T-pose. * If mesh and the normal map have the same location and direction, it may cause overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Be careful not to overlap the mesh. * It is highly recommended to create and apply the avatar's various items, such as shoes, hair, earrings, etc., as separate assets instead of including them in the AVT file. * The scanned data is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. * The number of meshes can impact the speed of CLO, so it is strongly recommended to create an avatar using a maximum of **70,000 triangles.** * Unless you intended to model Avatar asymmetrically, we recommend creating Avatar's mesh and joint symmetrically. * To fully utilize CLO / Marvelous Designer's Avatar IK feature, make sure that the joints' names and structure align with CLO/Marvelous Designer's Avatar. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775497351577) **** **2\. IMPORT AVATAR** Import the avatar files in the following formats into the Avatar Type: OBJ, DAE, FBX, GLTF ![제목 없음-1.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775561384473) **▶ Basic** * Load Type: Open * Object type: Avatar * Scale: Adjust the scale of Avatar. **▶Object** * Camera: Check whether to import camera data or camera animation data. * Joint Animation: Check whether to import animation data. * Cache Animation(MC): Check whether to import Cache Animation (MC) data. **▶Option** * Auto Add Arrangement Points: Automatically generate Arrangement Points and Bounding Volumes. * Auto Create Fitting Suit: Automatically generate a Fitting Suit for the avatar. **※ Note:** It is strongly recommended to check 'Auto Add Arrangement Points' and 'Auto Create Fitting Suit' when importing. * Move Garment to Start Position: Adjust the position of the garment to the starting point of the motions. **▶Axis Conversion** : adjust the axis of the Avatar. **▶Translation** * Align Bottom to Ground: Adjust the position of the avatar to be placed on the ground. **▶OK / Cancel** * Press 'OK' to import the Avatar, or press 'Cancel' to re-import the file to be used as the avatar. **3\. Bounding Volume & Arrangement Points ** To dress the garment on the AVATAR, a process called '**Positioning** ' is needed. To carry out the '**Positioning** ' process, it is necessary to generate and modify the BOUNDING VOLUME and ARRANGEMENT POINT. **※ Note:** You can automatically generate both Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points by selecting '**Auto Add Arrangement Points'** during import. **3-1. Creating and Modifying Bounding Volume & Arrangement Points** 1\. from the Main Menu > AVATAR > AVATAR EDITOR 2\. Click **Arrangement Tab** Please refer to the manuals below: * **[Bounding Volume](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000431228-Add-Edit-Bounding-Volume)** * **[Arrangement Point](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000430768-Add-Arrangement-Point)** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775497585945) **4\. FITTING SUIT** The**'Fitting Suit'** is a fitting dummy generated by referring to avatars with various sizes and shapes, enabling automatic dressing by auto-grading garments onto the avatar. **※ Note:** You can automatically generate a fitting suit by selecting **'Auto Create Fitting Suit'** during import. If the **'Fitting Suit'** is not positioned correctly, please generate it manually. **4-1. Creating Fitting Suit** 1\. From the Main Menu > AVATAR > AVATAR EDITOR 2\. Click **FITTING SUIT Tab** Please refer to the manuals below: * **[Fitting Suit](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/24451580024601-Create-the-Avatar-Fitting-Suit-ver-7-3)** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775513153689) **5\. Modifying AVATAR's Material** If you want to modify the textures and materials applied to AVATAR, you can adjust them in the Property Editor. 1\. Click the Avatar (AVT) in 3D Window 2\. Apply the textures and materials in the Property Editor. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775529091481) **6\. Save as AVT** Save the AVT file with both textures and materials applied. 1\. from the Main Menu, File > Save As > AVATAR ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775529415065) 2\. After specifying the file name and directory path, click Save (S). **7\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the AVT to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775555464985) **1\. UPLOAD****(Mandatory)**** ** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE****(Mandatory)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **3.****DESCRIPTION** please specify the following information on the Avatar file (AVT). * AVATAR HEIGHT (Scale Unit) * BUST CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * HIP CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * Presence of the JOINTS * Availability / Unavailability of CLO's AVATAR SIZING EDITOR * Compatibility / Incompatibility with CLO's default avatar ASSETS * Presence of the Magic Suit's Application Status **4\. TAGS** **'TAGS'** is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **5\. ATTACHMENT** You can attach files relating to the Avatar (AVT). However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to **'ATTACHMENT'** are being used. **6\. ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the AVT. **7\. THUMBNAIL** Register an image that well showcases the characteristics of the AVT. **Avatar thumbnails must be created with underwear worn** , and if nude images are used, item approval may be rejected. If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please register the rendered image. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process. **※ Note:** Avatar Item Approval will be rejected in the following Cases:
``` 1. Creating avatars using other 3D programs and converting them to different 3D formats or distributing them for commercial purposes. 2. Uploading avatars that have been plagiarized from other platforms or sites. 3. Content that triggers hatred. 4. Selling avatars provided by CLO or Marvelous Designer, either for free or for sale. 5. Using the specific person's name or infringing on portrait rights in avatars. 6. Providing nude images in thumbnails or on the detailed page.
```

title: Creating Zipper Bottom Stopper
content: **Zipper Structure![ziper_structure.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775849506841)** **Bottom Stopper** ※ Please check the requirements and recommendations for the Bottom stopper below. **[Required]** * The Bottom stopper(zipper) file format must be *ZSP or *ZST. * The Bottom(Open) Stopper is produced with two OBJs, while the Bottom(Closed) Stopper is produced with a single OBJ. * The OBJ should only contain the Stopper Mesh. * When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3 (100%). Please create the stopper file(OBJ) in size #3. * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. X-axis | Place the point where the zipper tape touches each stopper at the X-axis 0. ---|--- Y-axis | Top Stopper Position the point of the top stopper that aligns with the endpoint of the zipper tape at the Y-axis 0. Bottom Stopper Position the point of the bottom stopper that aligns with the bottom of the slider at the Y-axis 0. title: Referral Not Applied: Cases & Restrictions
content: ### How the Referral Feature Works When a friend enters CONNECT using your referral link, the referrer’s information is stored in the web browser’s cookies. ### When a Referral Cannot Be Established A referral relationship will **not** be created in the following cases: * A friend initially entered through one referrer’s link, but later signed up or made a purchase through another referrer’s link. * A friend enters through the referrer’s link but later uses a **different browser to purchase.** * A friend **deletes cookies** after entering through the referrer’s link. * Any other situation where the cookie-stored information cannot be retrieved. ### Prohibited Activities in Referral Programs The following actions are strictly prohibited while participating in the referral program: * Create a website that pretends to be CONNECT or replicates its design. * Share your referral link on illegal or unsafe websites. * Do anything that harms CONNECT’s reputation or brand image. * Use or share content that violates someone else’s copyright or the law. * Use illegal or unauthorized software that infringes CLO or Marvelous Designer’s rights. ### Losing Referrer Eligibility * Referrers who violate these policies will lose their eligibility. * Any earnings generated **after** losing eligibility will **not** be recognized.
content_description: This web page outlines the functionality, limitations, and prohibited activities of the referral feature in CONNECT, ensuring users understand how to effectively participate while maintaining compliance with program policies.

title: Referral Earnings Payout
content: ### When You Receive Earnings * Referral earnings are paid **the month after a sale occurs** , just like item sales. * For example, if a friend makes a purchase in January, your referral earnings will be paid at the **end of February**. * If an item is refunded, the earnings from that order will **not** be included. ### Minimum Payout Amount * Referral earnings are paid once your total earnings reach **$10 or more**.**(This calculation is based solely on referral earnings and is separate from item sales revenue.)** * Earnings below $10 will **accumulate** , and you will receive a payout in the month your total earnings reach $10 or more. ### How to Receive Your Earnings Earnings are automatically recorded, but you need to provide **payout information** to receive them. * Sellers who have already provided payout information for item sales **do not need to enter it again** — earnings will be paid automatically. * If you haven’t provided payout information yet, please follow the instructions below to register your **seller/payout information**. [Seller Info Registration](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/sections/44750777753497--Seller-Info-Registration)
content_description: This webpage provides essential information on how and when referral earnings are paid, including payout thresholds and instructions for submitting payout information.

title: Referral Earnings Status
content: ### When Do You Receive Referral Earnings? If a friend signs up through your referral link or makes their first paid purchase through your shared link, a **referral relationship** is established. If that friend then makes **any paid purchase within 60 days** of establishing the referral relationship, **10% of the purchase amount** will be credited to you as referral earnings. ### How to Check Your Referral Earnings 1. Click your **profile menu** on the right in CONNECT. 2. Click the **Sales** menu. 3. Select the **Referral** tab at the top. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/52811384718617) 4\. Under **Referral** , choose either the **Order** or **Payout** tab to view earnings by item. > Make sure the **date range** is set correctly when checking your referral earnings. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/52811384719257) #### **Checking Your Referral Status** You can find information about friends you have a referral relationship with and items sold during the selected period. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/52811429670169) **Invited Friends** * The number of friends with an active referral relationship during the selected period. * A friend is counted if **any part of their 60-day referral period** falls within the selected dates. **Items** * The total number of items purchased by your referred friends during the selected period. **Referral Revenue** * The total referral earnings for the selected period. * This equals **10% of the sales amount** of items purchased by your referred friends.

title: How the Referral Program Works - First Paid
content: #### **Eligible Referrals** * Friends who are registered but have never purchased a paid item. **(Existing User, no paid purchases)** #### **Establishing a Referral Relationship** * It can also begin when a friend who is already registered—but has never purchased a paid item—makes their first paid purchase through your shared link. * Once the referral relationship is established, it remains in effect for **60 days**. During this period, you’ll earn **10% of the friend’s total purchase amount** as your referral reward. #### **Referral Scenarios** **1)********First Paid Purchase:** When a new friend (Referee N), who is not registered, signs up on CONNECT using the link shared by an existing user (Referrer R), a referral relationship is established. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026457843225) **2)****Multiple Invitations:** Referee N may receive links from multiple Referrers, but **no referral relationship is established until they sign up**. If multiple Referrers send links, the referral relationship is **established only with the Referrer whose link the Referee used to sign up**. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026457845913) **3) After Referral is Established:** Once the referral relationship is established, receiving additional links from other referrers **will not change the existing relationship**. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026441168025) **4)****Earnings During Referral:** During the 60-day referral period, **10% of all paid purchases made by the friend(referree)** is credited to the referrer. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026441169177) **5)** **Referral Duration:** After 60 days, the referral relationship ends, and purchases made by the friend(referee) **will no longer be credited to the referrer.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026457856537)
content_description: This web page provides essential information on establishing and maximizing referral relationships, enabling users to earn rewards through friends' first paid purchases.
